source.title: 90% of US working hours are spent on tasks not covered well by AI benchmarks
source.author: speckx

title.zh: AI基准覆盖仅触及美国少数工作
title.en: AI Benchmark Coverage Misses Most US Work

excerpt.zh: AI基准覆盖研究显示，现有评测仅深入覆盖少数美国职业任务，约90%的工作时长仍缺乏充分基准支持。
excerpt.en: AI benchmark coverage research finds that current tests deeply cover only a small share of US job tasks, leaving about 90% of working hours poorly measured.

text.zh: AI基准覆盖远未代表真实工作
text.en: AI benchmark coverage falls short of real work

text.zh: AI基准覆盖研究由Mercor Research发布的一张“美国经济基准地图”显示，现有评测对真实经济活动的覆盖相当有限。研究将29个基准中的提示词映射到美国劳工部O*NET的923种职业和18,797项任务；只有208种职业拥有至少一项被5个或更多提示词覆盖的任务。研究据此估计，美国约90%的工作时长对应的任务几乎没有或没有现有基准覆盖。
text.en: A benchmark map from Mercor Research shows that AI benchmark coverage remains limited across real economic activity. The study maps prompts from 29 benchmarks onto 923 occupations and 18,797 tasks in the US Department of Labor’s O*NET taxonomy. Only 208 occupations have at least one task represented by five or more prompts, leading the researchers to estimate that roughly 90% of US working hours involve tasks with little or no current benchmark coverage.

text.zh: 覆盖集中在高曝光、高价值岗位
text.en: Coverage clusters around exposed, high-value work

text.zh: 覆盖并不是随机分布的。基准更偏向被认为容易受到AI影响的任务，也更常出现在工资总额较大的职业和被评为重要的任务中。因此，软件工程、金融分析和部分法律工作获得的测量更密集，而许多中等收入、规模较小的知识工作，以及卡车驾驶和工厂运营等领域则更容易成为盲区。这样的分布有其现实逻辑：有限的评测资源往往先投向最可能展示模型进展、且经济价值较高的任务。
text.en: Coverage is not distributed randomly. Benchmarks favor tasks considered more exposed to AI, occupations with larger wage bills, and tasks rated as important within those occupations. Software engineering, financial analysis, and some legal work therefore receive denser measurement, while many smaller middle-income knowledge jobs—as well as areas such as truck driving and plant operation—remain comparatively underrepresented. This allocation is understandable: limited evaluation resources tend to target tasks most likely to show model progress and economic value.

text.zh: AI基准地图的价值与边界
text.en: The value and limits of the AI benchmark map

text.zh: 这项工作的重要意义不在于给每个职业打出一个最终分数，而在于指出“我们还没有测量什么”。更完整的任务覆盖可以帮助企业判断模型是否适合具体流程，也能让政策制定者和求职者更谨慎地解读AI影响预测。它还提醒人们，简单平均相关基准成绩可能会过度强调被反复测试的少数任务，不能直接等同于模型在整份工作的表现。
text.en: The study’s main value is not assigning a final score to every occupation, but showing what has not yet been measured. Broader task coverage could help enterprises judge whether a model fits a particular workflow and give policymakers and workers a more grounded view of AI’s effects. It also warns against simply averaging scores from related benchmarks: that approach can overweight a small set of repeatedly tested tasks and should not be treated as a direct measure of performance across an entire job.

text.zh: 结论目前仍是阶段性的。研究只使用了首批29个基准，样本并不能完整代表所有公开、未饱和且具有经济真实性的评测；基准选择还包含难以完全形式化的主观判断。研究团队也承认，按职业类别限制基准数量虽然有助于扩大行业广度，却可能压低软件工程等热门领域的覆盖估计。随着基准库扩展，90%这一比例及覆盖格局都可能变化，因此它更适合作为研究缺口的警报，而不是AI能力的精确普查。
text.en: The conclusion is provisional. The analysis uses an initial set of 29 benchmarks, which cannot fully represent all public, unsaturated, economically realistic evaluations; some selection criteria also involve unavoidable judgment. The researchers note that capping benchmarks by job family broadens sector coverage but may understate coverage in heavily benchmarked areas such as software engineering. As the index grows, both the 90% estimate and the observed pattern may change, so the result is best read as a warning about measurement gaps rather than a precise census of AI capability.
